research_question: Does residual-based adaptive collocation improve PINN accuracy for transient convection-diffusion across Péclet numbers under an equal compute budget?
hypothesis: Pre-registered before execution (2026-11-02). Primary metric: relative L2 error on a 201x201 space-time grid vs the exact solution. H3.1: PINN error depends non-monotonically on Pe (U-shape): larger at Pe=1 (stiff initial diffusion layer) and at Pe=1000 (sharp transported pulse) than at Pe=10. H3.2: at equal collocation budget and iterations, residual-based adaptive samplers (RAD, R3) reduce rel. L2 vs fixed uniform sampling at Pe>=100; tested with paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests over seeds, Holm-corrected within each Pe (6 comparisons vs uniform), alpha=0.05. H3.3: at Pe<=10 no sampler differs significantly from uniform. H3.4 (ablation): Fourier features reduce error at Pe=1000; causal weighting reduces early-time error at Pe=1.
mathematical_formulation: u_t + u_x = Pe^-1 u_xx on periodic [0,1) x [0,1], u0 = Gaussian(x0=0.25, sigma0=0.1); exact solution by the method of images (physics.library.convdiff_exact)

model_configuration.arch: MLP 3x32 tanh, periodic embedding of x (hard periodic BC), soft IC

dataset_description: no data; exact reference solution (zero discretisation error up to image truncation < 1e-12)
limitations: budget equalised by points and iterations, not wall time; adaptive samplers spend extra residual evaluations (recorded)
